decisions.reason: It is a flagship reference electrometer close to the core dosimetry business, still featured on the home page, and costs little to keep, so the option stays open and is being exercised.

The risk management software extends the firm's QA offer and has kept its own page for two years; software upkeep is cheap and its value in patient-QA convergence is still unfolding, so keeping the option open makes sense.
The CT phantom was launched only recently, builds on the established imaging QA offer, and costs little to carry, so it is too early to abandon it.
The mammography phantom is distant from the core and its value is still uncertain, but it is cheap to keep after only one year, so the option should stay open while results come in.
This second mammography phantom overlaps with D and sits outside the core, which raises the chance of consolidation, but there is too little evidence yet to justify dropping a low-cost option.
This flagship imaging QA instrument line with several models represents the firm's strategic direction, so management is committing further to it rather than abandoning it.
